note: Shared by the CLI (bootstrap/interview.py) and the Worker UI (worker/src/interview.js). Plain language only. Every question has a recall prompt for people who do not know what they do not know, and clickable choices. 'phase' is the project-management lifecycle phase the answer feeds.

questions.ask: In a sentence or two, what do you want to exist?
recall: Picture it working. What is the first thing someone does with it?
What annoyed you enough to want this?
Think of one real person who would use it first.

questions.ask: Who else has a say or is affected?
recall: Who pays? Who approves? Who would complain if it broke?

questions.ask: How will you know it worked?
recall: What would you see or count a month after launch?
What number or moment would make you say yes, that is it?

questions.ask: What kind of thing is it mostly?
recall: Pick the closest. The system adds the rest.

choices.label: Something that runs by itself on a schedule

recall: Anything about people? Money? Files? Passwords?

choices.label: Names or contact details
choices.risk: Personal data: privacy rules and consent apply

choices.label: Payments
choices.risk: Payments: use a payment provider, never store card numbers

choices.label: Accounts and logins
choices.risk: Logins: use a hosted identity provider, never roll your own

questions.ask: What can it spend per month?
recall: Include model usage and hosting. Zero is a valid answer.

questions.ask: When do you want to see the first working version?
recall: A date helps the managers size the first step.

questions.ask: How should the work be run?
recall: Small steps you review often (agile), or a fixed plan with sign-offs (traditional)?

questions.ask: What must never happen without your say-so?
recall: Think of the worst surprise: a bill, a public post, a message to customers.
What would make you stop? What have you seen go wrong elsewhere?

questions.ask: How often do you want a short report?
recall: Reports are four lines. You only read them.

questions.ask: What does finished look like, and what happens to it afterwards?
recall: Who keeps it running? Is there a point where you would shut it down?
